Information since February indicates continued labor‑market strength, moderate growth, and inflation moving toward 2%, supporting the 25 bp hike within an overall accommodative stance and ongoing balance‑sheet reinvestments. Beige Book–style district reports are consistent with this: activity expanding at a modest-to-moderate pace, tight labor markets with only modest wage pressures, consumer spending steady but mixed with softer auto sales, and manufacturing generally stable to improving. Conditions in real estate are uneven—residential steady while some CRE segments show softening—which aligns with a cautious tone in property-related lending.

Incorporating credit conditions: the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows domestic banks keeping C&I standards broadly unchanged with expectations to ease somewhat as business loan demand strengthens, which supports investment; however, banks expect tighter standards for CRE (including construction/land development) and auto loans, and foresee deteriorating asset quality in credit cards, auto, and multifamily. Foreign banks report weaker business loan demand and plan tighter C&I/CRE standards. Mortgage standards remain largely unchanged for GSE‑eligible loans, with some improvement expected in nonconforming segments. Net effect: the credit channel is mixed—some support on the business side but caution in CRE and consumer credit—reinforcing the FOMC’s gradualism and data dependence and tempering the otherwise moderately positive tone.

Bottom line: The outlook remains moderately positive, but the mixed credit picture and uneven CRE conditions warrant a slightly less upbeat assessment than a purely macro read would suggest.
